answer: Price standing on a continuously-drained compute commitment. Each identity runs a verifiable proof-of-work heartbeat; the ledger scores the cumulative work integral since enrollment, not the instantaneous rate, smoothed by a trust kernel. A velvet-rope admission layer rejects any newcomer whose integral is below a floor. One operator cloning many identities must sustain N independent work streams on finite hardware, so each clone's integral grows by only its thin slice: the delta between an honest node's full stream and a starved clone's widens each epoch.
